intro.title: Test Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses a test context to isolate and verify its behavior. You will learn how to set up a testing environment using Angular's TestBed to configure dependencies and test components in isolation. The core concept is understanding how a test context provides a controlled environment for unit testing, ensuring your component works correctly without external interference. You will use key technologies like TypeScript, Jasmine for testing syntax, and Angular's testing utilities to write and run your tests.
intro.usecase: Test Context is essential for isolating component behavior in complex Angular applications like e-commerce dashboards, where you need to test product filters without loading the entire inventory system. Developers use it to mock dependencies like authentication services when testing user profile forms, ensuring login logic works independently of backend APIs. This pattern appears in admin panels where you test data table sorting without connecting to live databases, or in interactive UI components like modals that require specific context to validate user interactions. By creating focused test environments, developers can verify individual features work correctly before integrating them into the full application.
